svg.title: Y-V advancement geometry
svg.desc: A triangular tongue of tissue slides along the stem of a Y incision so the closure forms a V, redistributing local tissue. Advancement does not imply a universal length gain. The original running Y-V burn-scar technique is distinct from other GU Y-V and cutaneous V-Y variants. View: Generic cutaneous advancement, conceptual plan view. Scale: Conceptual schematic; not to scale. Units: No measured geometry; any dimensions are illustrative. Clinical review pending; no named clinician has signed off. Concept sources: Olbrisch: running Y-V plasty (1991 original technical article), https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1994813/; access: abstract checked; Advancement by sliding tissue on its bed in burn-scar treatment; do not equate every GU Y-V variant or V-Y flap. WARWIKI original vector schematic; individual illustrator not recorded. No separate figure reuse license recorded; linked sources are concept references, not artwork licenses.
